A Participant&#8217;s right to purchase shares of Common Stock under the Plan shall be exercisable only during the Participant&#8217;s lifetime and only by him or her.</font></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;line-height:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;color:#082169;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Treatment of Non-U.S. Participants</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;line-height:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.4%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Participants who are paid in foreign currency and who contribute foreign currency to the Plan through payroll deductions, will have such contributions converted to U.S. dollars on a monthly basis. The exchange rate for such conversion will be the rate quoted by a major financial institution selected by the Committee in its sole discretion. If the exchange rate for certain countries cannot be quoted in this manner, the conversion rate shall be determined as prescribed by the Committee. In no event will any procedure implemented for dealing with exchange rate fluctuations that may occur during the Purchase Period result in a purchase price below the price determined pursuant to Section 9 hereof.</p>

Any brokerage fees for the sale of shares of Common Stock purchased under the Plan shall be paid by each Participant.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;line-height:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.4%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All eligible Employees will have equal rights and privileges with respect to the Plan so that the Plan qualifies as an &#8220;employee stock purchase plan&#8221; within the meaning of Section 423 or any successor provision of the Code and related regulations. Any provision of the Plan that is inconsistent with Section 423 or any successor provision of the Code will, without further act or amendment by the Company, be reformed to comply with the requirements of Section 423. This Section 18 supersedes all other provisions in the Plan.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;line-height:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.4%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A Participant will have no rights as a stockholder under any election to purchase Common Stock until he or she becomes a stockholder of Schlumberger Limited as herein provided. A Participant will become a stockholder with respect to shares of Common Stock for which payment has been completed as provided in Section 9 hereof at the close of business on the last business day of the Purchase Period.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;line-height:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(a)</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:10pt;line-height:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;">Changes in Capitalization</font>. Subject to any required action by the stockholders of Schlumberger Limited, the right to purchase shares of Common Stock covered by a current Purchase Period and the number of shares of Common Stock that have been authorized for issuance under the Plan for any future Purchase Period, the maximum number of shares of Common Stock each Participant may purchase each Purchase Period pursuant to Section 9 hereof, as well as the price per share of Common Stock and the number of shares of Common Stock covered by each right under the Plan that have not yet been purchased shall be proportionately adjusted for any increase or decrease in the number of issued shares of Common Stock resulting from a stock split, reverse stock split, stock dividend, combination or reclassification of the Common Stock, or any other increase or decrease in the number of shares of Common Stock effected without receipt of consideration by the Company. Except as expressly provided herein, no issuance by the Company of shares of stock of any class, or securities convertible into shares of stock of any class, will affect, and no adjustment by reason thereof will be made with respect to, the number or price of shares of Common Stock.</p></td></tr></table></div>

In the event of the proposed dissolution or liquidation of Schlumberger Limited, the Purchase Period then in progress shall be shortened by setting a new Purchase Date (the &#8220;New Purchase Date&#8221;), and shall terminate immediately prior to the consummation of such proposed dissolution or liquidation, unless provided otherwise by the Board. The New Purchase Date will be before the date of the proposed dissolution or liquidation. Each Participant will be notified in writing, at least thirty (30) business days prior to the New Purchase Date, that the Purchase Date for the Participant&#8217;s right to purchase shares of Common Stock has been changed to the New Purchase Date and that the applicable number of shares of Common Stock will automatically be purchased on the New Purchase Date, unless prior to such date the Participant has withdrawn from the Plan as provided in Section 10 hereof. </p></td></tr></table></div>

In the event that the successor entity refuses to assume or substitute, or to cause a parent or subsidiary corporation to assume or substitute, the right to purchase shares of Common Stock, or is unable to assume or substitute such right in a manner compliant with Section 423 of the Code, then any Purchase Period then in progress shall be shortened by setting a new Purchase Date (the &#8220;Alternate Purchase Date&#8221;) and any Purchase Period then in progress will end on the Alternate Purchase Date. The Alternate Purchase Date shall be before the date of the proposed sale or merger. Each </p></td></tr></table></div>

<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Accumulated change in equity from transactions and other events and circumstances from non-owner sources, net of tax effect, at period end. Excludes Net Income (Loss), and accumulated changes in equity from transactions resulting from investments by owners and distributions to owners. Includes foreign currency translation items, certain pension adjustments, unrealized gains and losses on certain investments in debt and equity securities, other than temporary impairment (OTTI) losses related to factors other than credit losses on available-for-sale and held-to-maturity debt securities that an entity does not intend to sell and it is not more likely than not that the entity will be required to sell before recovery of the amortized cost basis, as well as changes in the fair value of derivatives related to the effective portion of a designated cash flow hedge.</p></div>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_StockholdersEquity">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Total of all stockholders' equity (deficit) items, net of receivables from officers, directors, owners, and affiliates of the entity which are attributable to the parent. The amount of the economic entity's stockholders' equity attributable to the parent excludes the amount of stockholders' equity which is allocable to that ownership interest in subsidiary equity which is not attributable to the parent (noncontrolling interest, minority interest). This excludes temporary equity and is sometimes called permanent equity.</p></div>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December&#160;31, 2020, Schlumberger contributed its onshore hydraulic fracturing business in the United States and Canada, including its pressure pumping, pumpdown perforating and Permian frac sand business to Liberty Energy Inc. (&#8220;Liberty&#8221;) in exchange for an equity interest in Liberty.&#160;During the first quarter of 2022, Schlumberger sold 7.2&#160;million of its shares of Liberty and received proceeds of $84 million.&#160;&#160;During the second quarter of 2022, Schlumberger sold an additional 26.5 million of its shares in Liberty and received proceeds of $429 million.&#160;&#160;As a result of these transactions Schlumberger recognized a gain of $26 million during the first quarter of 2022 and a gain of $216 million during the second quarter of 2022.&#160;As of June 30, 2022, Schlumberger had a 12% equity interest in Liberty.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the second quarter of 2022, Schlumberger sold certain real estate and received proceeds of $120 million.&#160;&#160;As a result of this transaction, Schlumberger recognized a gain of $43 million.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger did not record any charges or credits during the first six months of 2021.</p>

<span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger has a &#8364;750 million <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000687">three-year</span> committed revolving credit facility maturing in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000688">June 2024</span>.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2022 no amounts had been drawn under this facility.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition to the revolving credit facility described above, at June 30, 2022, Schlumberger had separate committed credit facility agreements aggregating $5.75 billion with commercial banks, all of which was available and unused. &#160;These committed facilities support commercial paper programs in the United States and Europe, of which $0.75 billion matures in February 2024, $2.0 billion matures in February 2025, $1.0 billion matures in July 2026 and $2.0 billion matures in February 2027.&#160;&#160;Interest rates and other terms of borrowing under these lines of credit vary by facility.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no borrowings under the commercial paper programs at June 30, 2022 and December 31, 2021.&#160;&#160;<span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span>  </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger Limited fully and unconditionally guarantees the securities issued by certain of its subsidiaries, including securities issued by Schlumberger Investment SA and Schlumberger Finance Canada Ltd., both wholly-owned subsidiaries of Schlumberger.</p><span></span>

<th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">6 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Jun. 30, 2022</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureAbstract', window );"><strong>Derivative Instruments And Hedging Activities Disclosure [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock', window );">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</a></td>
<td class="text">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8.&#160;&#160; <span style="text-decoration:underline;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</span> </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a multinational company, Schlumberger conducts its business in over 120 countries.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#8217;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; </span>Amounts recorded in<span style="font-style:italic;"> Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss </span>are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; </p>


<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160; Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks.&#160; Included in <span style="font-style:italic;">Other Liabilities</span> was $<span style="color:#000000;">266</span> million at June 30, 2022 ($78 million at December 31, 2021), and included in <span style="font-style:italic;">Other Assets</span> at December 31, 2021 was $66 million relating to the fair value of outstanding cross-currency swap derivatives.&#160; The fair value was determined using a model with inputs that are observable in the market or can be derived or corroborated by observable data.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2019, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#8364;1.5 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#8364;1.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#8364;0.5 billion 0.00% Notes due 2024, &#8364;0.5 billion 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#8364;0.5 billion 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 2.29%, 2.51% and 2.76%, respectively.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#8364;0.8 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#8364;0.8 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#8364;0.4 billion of 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#8364;0.4 billion of 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 1.87% and 2.20%, respectively. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#8364;2.0 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#8364;2.0 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#8364;1.0 billion of 1.375% Guaranteed Notes due 2026 and &#8364;1.0 billion of 2.00% Guaranteed Notes due 2032.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the swapped portion of the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 2.77% and 3.49%, respectively.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2020, a Canadian dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued $0.5 billion of US dollar denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of $0.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its $0.5 billion 1.40% Senior Notes due 2025.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the US dollar notes to Canadian dollar denominated debt with a fixed annual interest rate of 1.73%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the fourth quarter of 2021 and the first quarter of 2022, Schlumberger entered into derivative contracts that hedge the price of oil relating to approximately 75% of the projected oil production for all of 2022 and a portion of the production for the first quarter of&#160;&#160;2023 of one of its Asset Performance Solutions (&#8220;APS&#8221;) projects. These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in fair value of the hedge recorded in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</span>. Amounts recorded in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accumulated other comprehensive loss</span> are reclassified to earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings. At June 30, 2022, included in <span style="font-style:italic;">Accounts payable and accrued liabilities</span> was $71 million and included in <span style="font-style:italic;">Other current assets was </span>$5 million relating to the fair value of the outstanding commodity contracts. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Schlumberger is exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;While Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes.&#160;&#160;Instead, the fair value of the contracts is recorded on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Balance Sheet </span>and changes in the fair value are recognized in the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income, </span>as are changes in the fair value of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At June 30, 2022, contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $7.3 billion in various foreign currencies, of which $5.7 billion relates to hedges of debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other than the previously mentioned cross-currency swaps and commodity hedges, the fair value of the other outstanding derivatives was not material at June 30, 2022 and December 31, 2021. </p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The effect of derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges, and those not designated as hedges, on the <span style="font-style:italic;">Consolidated Statement of Income </span>was as follows: </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for loss and gain contingencies. Describes any existing condition, situation, or set of circumstances involving uncertainty as of the balance sheet date (or prior to issuance of the financial statements) as to a probable or reasonably possible loss incurred by an entity that will ultimately be resolved when one or more future events occur or fail to occur, and typically discloses the amount of loss recorded or a range of possible loss, or an assertion that no reasonable estimate can be made.</p></div>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for reporting segments including data and tables. Reportable segments include those that meet any of the following quantitative thresholds a) it's reported revenue, including sales to external customers and intersegment sales or transfers is 10 percent or more of the combined revenue, internal and external, of all operating segments b) the absolute amount of its reported profit or loss is 10 percent or more of the greater, in absolute amount of 1) the combined reported profit of all operating segments that did not report a loss or 2) the combined reported loss of all operating segments that did report a loss c) its assets are 10 percent or more of the combined assets of all operating segments.</p></div>

&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;On December&#160;31, 2020, Schlumberger contributed its onshore hydraulic fracturing business in the United States and Canada, including its pressure pumping, pumpdown perforating and Permian frac sand business to Liberty Energy Inc. (&#x201c;Liberty&#x201d;) in exchange for an equity interest in Liberty.&#160;During the first quarter of 2022, Schlumberger sold 7.2&#160;million of its shares of Liberty and received proceeds of $84 million.&#160;&#160;During the second quarter of 2022, Schlumberger sold an additional 26.5 million of its shares in Liberty and received proceeds of $429 million.&#160;&#160;As a result of these transactions Schlumberger recognized a gain of $26 million during the first quarter of 2022 and a gain of $216 million during the second quarter of 2022.&#160;As of June 30, 2022, Schlumberger had a 12% equity interest in Liberty.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the second quarter of 2022, Schlumberger sold certain real estate and received proceeds of $120 million.&#160;&#160;As a result of this transaction, Schlumberger recognized a gain of $43 million.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger did not record any charges or credits during the first six months of 2021.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger has a &#x20ac;750 million &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000687"&gt;three-year&lt;/span&gt; committed revolving credit facility maturing in &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000688"&gt;June 2024&lt;/span&gt;.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2022 no amounts had been drawn under this facility.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:2pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;In addition to the revolving credit facility described above, at June 30, 2022, Schlumberger had separate committed credit facility agreements aggregating $5.75 billion with commercial banks, all of which was available and unused. &#160;These committed facilities support commercial paper programs in the United States and Europe, of which $0.75 billion matures in February 2024, $2.0 billion matures in February 2025, $1.0 billion matures in July 2026 and $2.0 billion matures in February 2027.&#160;&#160;Interest rates and other terms of borrowing under these lines of credit vary by facility.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;There were no borrowings under the commercial paper programs at June 30, 2022 and December 31, 2021.&#160;&#160;&lt;span style="font-size:12pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;  &lt;/p&gt;

    <us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock contextRef="C_0000087347_20220101_20220630" id="F_000447">
&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;8.&#160;&#160; &lt;span style="text-decoration:underline;"&gt;Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;As a multinational company, Schlumberger conducts its business in over 120 countries.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger&#x2019;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar.&#160;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks.&#160; These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in the fair value of the hedge recorded on the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet &lt;/span&gt;and in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss.&#160; &lt;/span&gt;Amounts recorded in&lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt; Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss &lt;/span&gt;are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&#160; &lt;/p&gt;


&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is also exposed to risks on future cash flows relating to certain of its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160; Schlumberger uses cross-currency swaps to provide a hedge against these cash flow risks.&#160; Included in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other Liabilities&lt;/span&gt; was $&lt;span style="color:#000000;"&gt;266&lt;/span&gt; million at June 30, 2022 ($78 million at December 31, 2021), and included in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other Assets&lt;/span&gt; at December 31, 2021 was $66 million relating to the fair value of outstanding cross-currency swap derivatives.&#160; The fair value was determined using a model with inputs that are observable in the market or can be derived or corroborated by observable data.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During 2019, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;1.5 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;1.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.00% Notes due 2024, &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;0.5 billion 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 2.29%, 2.51% and 2.76%, respectively.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;0.8 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160;&#160;Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;0.8 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;0.4 billion of 0.25% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;0.4 billion of 0.50% Notes due 2031.&#160;&#160;These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 1.87% and 2.20%, respectively. &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued &#x20ac;2.0 billion of Euro-denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of &#x20ac;2.0 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 1.375% Guaranteed Notes due 2026 and &#x20ac;1.0 billion of 2.00% Guaranteed Notes due 2032.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the swapped portion of the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of 2.77% and 3.49%, respectively.&#160; &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During 2020, a Canadian dollar functional currency subsidiary of Schlumberger issued $0.5 billion of US dollar denominated debt.&#160; Schlumberger entered into cross-currency swaps for an aggregate notional amount of $0.5 billion in order to hedge changes in the fair value of its $0.5 billion 1.40% Senior Notes due 2025.&#160; These cross-currency swaps effectively convert the US dollar notes to Canadian dollar denominated debt with a fixed annual interest rate of 1.73%.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;During the fourth quarter of 2021 and the first quarter of 2022, Schlumberger entered into derivative contracts that hedge the price of oil relating to approximately 75% of the projected oil production for all of 2022 and a portion of the production for the first quarter of&#160;&#160;2023 of one of its Asset Performance Solutions (&#x201c;APS&#x201d;) projects. These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the changes in fair value of the hedge recorded in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Accumulated other comprehensive loss&lt;/span&gt;. Amounts recorded in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Accumulated other comprehensive loss&lt;/span&gt; are reclassified to earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings. At June 30, 2022, included in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Accounts payable and accrued liabilities&lt;/span&gt; was $71 million and included in &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other current assets was &lt;/span&gt;$5 million relating to the fair value of the outstanding commodity contracts. &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Schlumberger is exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities denominated in currencies other than the functional currency.&#160;&#160;While Schlumberger uses foreign currency forward contracts to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes.&#160;&#160;Instead, the fair value of the contracts is recorded on the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet &lt;/span&gt;and changes in the fair value are recognized in the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income, &lt;/span&gt;as are changes in the fair value of the hedged item.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;At June 30, 2022, contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $7.3 billion in various foreign currencies, of which $5.7 billion relates to hedges of debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. &lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;Other than the previously mentioned cross-currency swaps and commodity hedges, the fair value of the other outstanding derivatives was not material at June 30, 2022 and December 31, 2021. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"&gt;The effect of derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges, and those not designated as hedges, on the &lt;span style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income &lt;/span&gt;was as follows: &lt;/p&gt;
